content.overview: Section 128 requires every company to keep books of account and other relevant books and papers at its registered office. The books are kept on accrual basis and according to the double-entry system, and give a true and fair view. They are preserved for eight financial years.
content.glance: Section 128 requires every company to keep proper books of account and other relevant papers at its registered office, on accrual basis and double-entry system.
content.study:
## Statutory rule
Section 128(1) requires every company to prepare and keep at its registered office books of account and other relevant books and papers and financial statements for every financial year which give a true and fair view of the state of the affairs of the company, including that of its branch office, and explain the transactions effected both at the registered office and its branches. The books are kept on accrual basis and according to the double-entry system of accounting.

The proviso lets the board keep the books at another place in India, after giving the Registrar notice.

Section 128(5) requires the books to be kept in good order for not less than eight financial years immediately preceding a financial year, or where the company has not been in existence for eight years, for the whole of that period.

## Answer structure
Name the place, the accrual and double-entry system, and the eight-year preservation. Not a verified closure.

sections.heading: Ingredient 1
sections.body: Books at registered office or intimated place

sections.heading: Rule
sections.body: Books must explain transactions, including at the registered office and branches, and give a true and fair view. They may be kept electronically in the manner prescribed. The default place is the registered office; another place in India needs a board resolution and intimation to the Registrar. Books of the preceding eight financial years, or such shorter life of the company, must be preserved. A director may inspect. Branch returns are sent periodically. Failure exposes managing director, whole-time director in charge of finance, CFO, and other persons charged by the board.
